name: Pakistani Haleem
description: Slow-cooked Pakistani beef haleem with wheat, barley and mixed lentils blended into a thick, cohesive texture and finished with classic fresh garnishes.
ingredients: 750 g beef, boneless or shank pieces
Salt to taste and cooking oil, as needed
Fried onions, julienned ginger, coriander and lemon for serving
method: Rinse the wheat, barley and lentils thoroughly and soak them for about 1 hour, then drain.
Cook the soaked grains and lentils in plenty of fresh water at a gentle simmer until they are extremely soft and can be mashed easily, adding hot water when needed to prevent scorching.

In another heavy pot, fry the onions in oil until golden. Add the ginger-garlic paste, beef, haleem masala, red chilli, turmeric and salt and cook until the meat is tender, adding water as required for the cut you use.
Remove any bones if using bone-in meat, shred the tender beef finely and return it to its masala.
Mash or blend the cooked grain-and-lentil mixture to your preferred smoothness, then combine it gradually with the shredded beef mixture.

Cook together on low heat, stirring and scraping the base frequently, until the haleem becomes thick, cohesive and glossy. Adjust with hot water if it becomes too stiff before the flavours have combined.
Taste for seasoning and serve hot with fried onions, julienned ginger, coriander and lemon.
